re-flora · Release evidence · 5 October 2026 · RTX 3060 Ti

Grass model pixelization:
what costs time, and what games actually do

Pixelization is not the main cost of the analytic reference. The current raster-grid backend adds substantial work to an already cheap continuous mesh renderer. Pixel-art appearance alone predicts neither result.

Correctness repaired · mass-grass performance acceptance still fails

1. Implemented and repaired

  • Vulkan reflection test: replaced the retired particle shader artifact with the active particle_billboard.vert; the test checks the live compact input and all instance/leaf formats, not just file existence.
  • Synchronization: acquire waits and acquired-image transitions share TRANSFER | COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT scope. Attachment dependencies include LOAD/blending reads and early/late depth use. The previous TOP_OF_PIPE transition could run before the acquire wait. Validation was not suppressed, and no global idle workaround was added. [S10]
  • Removed modes: tapered square and crossed ribbons are gone from active geometry, topology, buffers, GUI and fixtures. Original voxel, Analytic Reference and Square Color Bands remain. Legacy saved choices 2/3 normalize to Square in memory without resetting unrelated values.
  • One saved grass pixelization checkbox: now controls both analytic and square rendering. Unchecked means continuous sampling/depth; checked means model-grid sampling. The disabled analytic lattice has cell=0, making ray sampling and depth remapping genuine identities. A Slang regression reproduced the previous failure.
  • Additional stress failure found and fixed: 82,454 residents at resolution 128 exhausted the fixed Vulkan descriptor pool. Consecutive identical semantic bindings now reuse an immutable transient set within the current recording. Changed bindings still claim a distinct set; every batch still declares resource uses/barriers. We did not raise an arbitrary pool ceiling or drop plants.
Runtime A/B: enable experimental grass, choose Analytic Reference or Square Color Bands, then toggle Grass: model-grid pixelization (analytic and square stems) in Stem Model Pixelization. “Continuous” does not add anti-aliasing; it removes the explicit model grid. Flowers retain their separate controls; CPU climbing simulation/collision remain CPU-owned, and GPU grass stays GPU-owned. Flat final color/lighting per Band is preserved.

Matching near-camera crops

Actual Release captures, same camera/time/population. Identical 768×432 crop at (1664,160); no image processing beyond cropping. Geometry differs between analytic rounded stems and square tubes, so cross-geometry images are not equivalence claims.

2. Measurement contract

110 primary serial native runs across 11 camera/resolution cohorts; two opposite-order repeats and 592 frames per metric/mode/cohort. 40 additional diagnostic-suite runs include 8 square-grid runs with extra per-batch GPU timestamps. Quick checks, failed runs and pre-fix measurements are excluded from current tables.

Same Release binary at 562299a267a6952a91b7605b75338c8644010295; Linux/native Vulkan, NVIDIA RTX 3060 Ti (8 GiB), driver 580.159.04, Intel i5-12600KF, 2560×1440 physical window. Hidden/muted native surface/swapchain, fixed fixture clock, production painted grass, post-paint warmup, GPU pose reuse on. Primary comparisons disable phase diagnostics. Saved GUI/camera hashes remained identical. Existing user tuning was preserved rather than replaced with factory defaults.

  • 3×3 paint: 2,267 tall + 1,831 short = 4,098 residents. 15×15: 45,518 + 36,936 = 82,454. Residents are not a visible-plant count.
  • graphics.flora: drawing, or the complete grid backend including view preparation, tiles, display/fallback and pass restarts.
  • graphics.flora_lighting_cache: shared flora lighting and optional Band-pose preparation; not isolated grass-only compute.
  • grass.render_total: sum of those two scopes within each frame, then percentile; not the sum of separate medians. Initial pass setup remains in whole-frame timing.
  • cpu.record: entire render.trace_record, not grass-only CPU time. cpu.submit: render.submit_present, separate from recording/acquisition.
  • frame.render: whole GPU render scope, not uncapped whole-game FPS. Do not add CPU and GPU timings into a fabricated serial frame budget.

Committed measurement summary / p95 / hashes. Raw per-frame samples and logs remain in local target/ artifacts linked below. Timestamp scopes locate work regions; no Nsight hardware counters were captured.

At 82,454/wide, square-grid backend + shared prep is 7.152 ms: 3.92× continuous Square and 1.98× pixelized Analytic. CPU tracer recording is 4.445 vs 0.589 ms; whole GPU rendering is 11.523 vs 6.201 ms.

Plain Square is much cheaper than the analytic reference, but not automatically cheaper than original voxel grass. The atlas candidate retains the flat Band material yet adds work; its large-population regressions persist at the whole-GPU-frame level, not just in a narrowly named draw scope. CPU recording grows materially; submit/present is not the dominant added CPU cost.

4. Does quantization explain the analytic cost?

Feature ablation: same analytic geometry and lighting, model grid off/on
Residents / cameraContinuous backend, msGrid backend, msDifference of p50sIncrease
4,098 / near1.5541.9440.390 ms25.1%
82,454 / wide2.8443.0670.223 ms7.8%
82,454 / far4.0244.6310.607 ms15.1%
82,454 / low1.6451.7870.142 ms8.6%

This is now a real same-geometry feature ablation. Geometry, Band coloring and lighting remain analytic in both modes. The toggle changes lattice creation, proxy padding, sample-ray quantization and sampled-depth remapping together. It does not separately isolate arithmetic instructions from the extra proxy fragment footprint.

Most analytic cost remains with the grid off. The fragment shader still traces up to seven rounded-cone segments for each physical proxy fragment; neighboring output fragments can repeat the same quantized ray. Snapping a ray does not cache the intersection result or lower the main render-target resolution. The earlier “analytic versus plain mesh” comparison could not prove that pixelization caused the analytic expense.

At finer model-grid resolutions the analytic on/off gap contracts in the quality sweep. That is consistent with less proxy-padding/coverage inflation, but is not an instruction-counter proof. Intersection cost, proxy overdraw, interpolation and depth-export behavior remain separate profiling questions.

Determinism guard: with pixels off, all eight near-camera captures (two repeats × resolutions 16/45/128/512) are byte-identical for Analytic and Square. The original voxel control matches in 7/8 captures; one same-R45 repeat differs in 15 of 3,686,400 pixels (normalized RMSE 0.00000408). We do not claim universal original-renderer determinism. Hashes and the repeat exception are recorded in the committed JSON.

5. Grid density, distance and batching

Quality sweep, primary runs: p50 ms; larger R means finer model-grid sampling
Residents / camera / RReserved slot side / capacityAnalytic continuousAnalytic gridSquare grid backendSquare grid CPU record
82,454 / wide · R3264 / 10242.8463.1476.5674.385
82,454 / wide · R4564 / 10242.8443.0676.5294.445
82,454 / wide · R128256 / 642.8482.96345.14457.815
4,098 / near · R3264 / 10241.5322.1361.2560.947
4,098 / near · R4564 / 10241.5541.9441.2630.955
4,098 / near · R128256 / 641.5841.7455.6753.555
4,098 / near · R512512 / 161.5921.62413.64812.094

The atlas is fixed at 2048²: 64 MiB RGBA32F color/eye-depth + 16 MiB D32 tile depth = 80 MiB, allocated lazily and retained after switching off. Requested resolution reserves a power-of-two slot: effective R32 or R45 → 64² / 1,024 instances; R128 → 256² / 64; R512 → 512² / 16 per batch. The theoretical 32² minimum slot has capacity 4,096, but current saved resolution normalization does not select it.

Active rectangles can be smaller, and distance-dependent sampling LOD avoids oversampling tiny projected plants. That does not reduce the reserved slot or the CPU batch count. Higher requested density can therefore increase main-pass restarts and recording cost even where the useful samples are capped by screen footprint. Not every curve must be monotonic: coverage, LOD thresholds and power-of-two allocation steps matter.

Requested is not applied: the R32 cohorts originally requested 16, but StemExperiment.normalized() clamps to 32..512. The report records both and labels the applied R32 value. That explains why “R16” did not give a 4,096-instance batch or reduce CPU recording. The fixture and benchmark now normalize at the boundary and verify the renderer's logged resolution, so future metadata cannot silently repeat this mistake.

The newly discovered R128 descriptor crash was a correctness limit, not a performance sample. It is retained only as red-gate evidence under target/stem-pixel-research/pre-descriptor-reuse/; every current table uses the repaired binary.

Analytic, continuousShared lighting → clipped proxy → intersection per physical fragment → exact hit depth
Analytic, gridShared lighting → padded model-grid proxy → quantized ray + repeated intersection → remapped sampled depth
Square, continuousShared lighting + GPU Band poses → instanced triangles → flat Band color + hardware depth
Square, gridShared lighting + poses → view/grid compute → [active-cell clear + tile mesh → sample display + continuous fallback + LOAD restarts] × bounded batches

82,454 / wide · R45842.178 / 2.4253.074 / 3.0961.475 / 1.5180.177 / 0.1966.896 / 7.375

The final display is not the whole regression. In the wide diagnostic, atlas clear/mesh/transitions take 3.074 ms and view preparation 2.178 ms, versus 1.475 ms for display/fallback. The far diagnostic's atlas interval rises to 5.828 ms while view preparation and display change much less. At near R512, batching grows from 8 to 259 intervals per frame and both preparation and atlas work expand. These are work-region observations, not proof of a particular hardware bottleneck.

Each phase name repeats per streamed batch. The script sums repeated scopes within the same frame before calculating percentiles; batches are not treated as independent frame samples. “View prep” includes compute and pre-atlas resource transitions; “atlas” includes clear/mesh and attachment transitions; “display” includes sampling/fallback and main-LOAD transitions.

The residual is the per-frame backend interval minus measured phase intervals, not an independently identified bandwidth or barrier bill. Table phase medians must not be added as if they were paired. Extra ALL_COMMANDS timestamps and batch logs can perturb scheduling/recording; phase numbers are diagnostic, while the earlier tables are primary acceptance evidence.

What is established: this backend adds grid preparation, wide color/depth data, repeated atlas/main passes, display sampling and substantial CPU recording. What is not established: the exact limiting hardware unit, clear-versus-mesh split, cache hit rate, VRAM bandwidth saturation, or early-Z rejection rate. NVIDIA recommends unit/counter analysis; AMD's export/attachment advice motivates experiments but does not diagnose this NVIDIA GPU. [S7] [S8]

7. “Pixel art should be cheap” conflates different strategies

Released-game evidence describes different pipelines, not interchangeable GPU benchmarks
GameWhat its developer actually describesWhat we can conclude
Dead Cells [S1]3D animation tools export tiny non-AA sprite frames and normal maps.Primarily an offline production/iteration strategy; it does not run our per-plant atlas at play time.
A Short Hike [S2] [S2b]A low-resolution whole-world RenderTexture; flat shading, outlines, no AA, adjustable pixel size.Can reduce scene pixel work. This is not a private model grid for each plant; no matched GPU timing is published in these accounts.
Return of the Obra Dinn [S3] [S3b]3D grayscale rendering, then 1-bit conversion; shipped 800×450 scene rendering with stabilized dithering.The 1-bit appearance is an output treatment, not a claim that all intermediates/calculations are 1-bit or free.
Prodeus [S4] [S4b] [S4c]Retro visuals combined with modern 3D/effects; developer performance advice targets resolution, SSR and SSAO.Art style does not erase effect costs. The 2021 support advice predates the September 2022 1.0 release; it is not a final-release A/B benchmark or proof of a specific pixelizer.

No game FPS or milliseconds were invented. These checked sources provide implementation or production accounts, not a controlled benchmark of our model-local renderer. The A Short Hike thread is a mirrored developer statement; Prodeus's reply was verified against its actual developer badge and comment ID. Readable fetches omitted those passages, so raw bodies were checked. See the source ledger for evidence boundaries.

Four costs that the same appearance can hide

  1. Offline sprites: expensive model animation/rendering can happen during authoring. Runtime sprite work is a different comparison; deformation/view freedom is constrained.
  2. Lower-resolution scene rendering: scaling both target dimensions by s yields s² target pixels. It can remove resolution-dependent shading, but not proportionally reduce CPU, vertex, simulation or shared preparation. Unity documents render-scale and upscaling as a target-resolution strategy. [S5] [S6]
  3. Full-resolution snapping or post-treatment: rounding coordinates alone does not reduce fragment invocation count; a final filter can add work unless it replaces more expensive work.
  4. Per-model grids: preserve independent object-local samples/silhouettes/depth, but need sample generation, storage and composition. This is our square-grid path; it is not equivalent to merely lowering the whole scene resolution.

Our continuous Square fragment already emits one prepared Band color. There is no expensive smooth material/lighting shader for pixelization to replace. The aesthetic is not the workload: work avoided must exceed work added. Extra intermediate targets, cameras/passes and exports deserve measurement, not stylistic assumptions. [S6b]

8. Recommendations and limits

  1. Keep continuous Square and original voxel available. Do not migrate mass grass to the atlas candidate or treat the visual candidate as performance acceptance. The shared checkbox provides the requested honest visual comparison.
  2. Profile the largest measured region with hardware counters. Capture Nsight GPU Trace on this GPU before choosing ALU, texture, ROP or bandwidth optimizations. Account separately for CPU recording and GPU critical-path effects. [S7]
  3. Reduce redundant view/bounds preparation and prototype GPU visibility/resolution worklists with fewer pass restarts. Reserved-size bucketing and compacted visible instances may reduce wasted batching. Keep GPU ownership, conservative near/eye clipping, growth and all visible plants; no CPU readback or dropped-plant workaround.
  4. Experiment with cheaper sample storage only after precision checks. The atlas stores full float color/eye depth plus hardware tile depth. Packing or narrower color can save data, but must preserve flat Band color/HDR, occlusion and near-camera depth. Enlarging the atlas trades VRAM for batches, not a free fix. [S8]
  5. Treat depth-export optimizations as proof obligations. Conservative depth qualifiers require a valid bound relative to rasterizer depth; blindly removing sampled depth or forcing early tests changes visibility. No early-Z bottleneck has been demonstrated here. [S9]

These are unimplemented next experiments, not claimed speedups. A fullscreen low-resolution fallback would be a different visual contract. Cross-platform performance, universal analytic/raster pixel-depth equivalence, shadow equivalence and temporal appearance approval are not established. Eye-plane singularities retain continuous mesh fallback and sampling LOD can differ from analytic. Visual review remains separate from later performance acceptance.

Use --help for supported scenes, limits, recovery and artifact naming. Very large diagnostic sweeps fail if the 1,024-scope pool drops timestamps; reduce population/density, do not accept partial attribution. Primary runs do not enable those extra queries.

Final gates: formatting/check, root Rust tests, full Vulkan tests, 35 Slang CPU tests, native hidden Release smoke/log inspection, and five explicit synchronization fixtures (startup, resize, analytic lifecycle, square-grid lifecycle, 82,454/R128 descriptor stress). No suppressed hazards/errors, and clean shutdown. Passed: 1,365 Rust tests + four CLI tests (four ignored), 57 Vulkan tests, 35 Slang tests, all five synchronization fixtures, four CPU path fixtures and actual climbing prune/wait/regrow/root-recovery with nonzero square-stem drawing. Final validation used f8b5298d; the later fixture-normalization change does not change rendering. Counts/log paths are in the committed measurement JSON.
